title: What's New: Resource Governance for Business Central Online (2023 release wave 2)

chapters.title: Resource governance mission and optimal consumption
Quotas vs limits - concepts and differences
History of resource governance and consumption tracking
Key operational limits and entitlement quotas introduction
Operational limits concepts and highway analogy
Speed limit in Business Central Online
Concurrency limit and execution time limit
Scheduled task and web service request improvements
Web service concurrency and execution time limits

features.name: Entitlement quotas
features.description: A new concept of quotas that will be introduced to allow customers and users to claim or exercise their entitlement rights based on their licenses. These quotas are tiered by license type, cumulative per environment, but non-transferable between users.
features.status_evidence_quote: we are planning to introduce this concept of quotas in the next uh uh few seme from now
caveats: Estimated for next two or three quarters
99% of customers expected to stay within quota

features.name: Operational limits
features.description: Fixed rules that apply equally to all users and are non-transferable. These govern how fast resources can be consumed and protect the service from unfair usage.

features.name: Resource consumption tracking
features.description: A system that tracks all types of workloads and capacity units including number of tasks, requests, sessions, execution time, memory, and storage consumption per user, environment, and customer at any given moment and period.

features.name: Local consumption tracker
features.description: A service that tracks resource consumption per user and per environment in each cluster to implement operational limits.

features.name: Global consumption tracker
features.description: A service that aggregates resource consumption from local consumption trackers in each cluster across the whole tenant and applies customer-wide quotas.

features.name: User-based operational limits
features.description: A clear user-based limit that will be published to protect the service, ensure fairness among users, and inspire elasticity and scalability. Previously most limits were environment-based.

features.name: Dynamic resource-based limits
features.description: Internal limits applied under the hood to ensure the service is scalable, protected, and ensures fairness among customers and environments. Not published to end users.

features.name: Intelligent workload balancing
features.description: Improved elasticity technique that uses consumption patterns and limit exhaustion signals to distribute and rebalance workloads more intelligently across hosts, grouping heavy and light consuming tenants to balance each other.

features.name: Entitlement quotas and flexible access consumption
features.description: Publishing user-based and tenant-wide quotas for licensed and unlicensed users, and allowing customers to buy additional add-on capacity or pay-as-you-go for excess consumption.
caveats: Estimated for next two or three quarters
99% of customers expected to stay within quota

features.name: Speed limit for web service requests
features.description: Changing the speed limit from 600 requests per environment per minute to 6,000 requests per user in a 5-minute sliding window, providing flexibility for burst peaks.

features.name: Scheduled task concurrency limit increase
features.description: Upgrading the concurrency limit for scheduled tasks from 3 concurrently running tasks per environment to 5 concurrently running tasks per user.
features.status_evidence_quote: so the preview that's coming this next quarter is first um in the early um uh early quarter

features.name: Web service request concurrency limit per user
features.description: Changing the web service request concurrency limit from 10 concurrently handled requests per environment to 10 concurrently handled requests per user, maintaining 5 processed and 95 queued ratio.

features.name: Execution time limit for workloads
features.description: Introducing a new limit to control how long workloads can process in the system, based on server cores and elapsed time sliding windows, with environment limits underneath.
features.status_evidence_quote: in the future you can expect the introduction of the execution time limit that I mentioned before

features.name: Gradual throughput increase during preview
features.description: Implementing operational limits with gradual throughput increases throughout the preview period rather than big bang changes, with continuous monitoring and fine-tuning.
